# SQL*Plus

Oracle's command-line client, and the execution model the whole of
[[oracle-database-laboratories]] is written against. Every script in that repo is a SQL*Plus script
first and a SQL file second — the `@` run order, the `&` substitution variables and the `/` statement
terminator are all client features, not database ones.

## The four client features the repo depends on

| Feature | Use |
|---|---|
| `@path/to/script.sql` | run a file; the README's run order is literally a list of `@` lines |
| `&variable` | prompt-and-substitute at parse time — the repo's only parameterisation mechanism |
| `SET SERVEROUTPUT ON` | make `DBMS_OUTPUT.PUT_LINE` actually print; without it the block runs and shows nothing |
| `SHOW ERRORS PACKAGE BODY x` | see why a body compiled invalid |
| `/` on its own line | terminate a PL/SQL block or type body — a bare `;` will not |

`SET SERVEROUTPUT ON` appears at the top of every procedural script. Forgetting it is the classic
"my trigger did nothing" false alarm: the code ran, the buffer filled, nothing was flushed.

## Substitution variables versus bind variables

`&name` is a **textual** substitution performed by the client before the statement reaches the server.
It is not a bind variable: there is no type, no reuse of the parsed plan, and no protection against
whatever the value expands into. Host binds (`:name`) exist, but need a separate `VARIABLE`
declaration before the block will run.

The repo standardises on substitution throughout and says so where the choice is visible:

> "Substitution variables (&...) throughout, consistent with the rest of the file -- mixing in a host
> bind (:name) would need a separate VARIABLE declaration before the block would run under SQL*Plus."
> — Oracle-Database-Laboratories/sql/03_plsql/02_cursors.sql, 2026-07-25

That records *internal consistency* as the reason for the choice, which is real but narrow.

## Output is deliberately not committed

`.gitignore` excludes `*.lst`, `*.log`, `*.trc`, `sqlnet.log` and `afiedt.buf` — SQL*Plus spool and
editor artefacts — alongside wallet and credential material (`*.sso`, `*.p12`, `*.jks`,
`tnsnames.ora`, `wallet/`). Clean, but it has a consequence the wiki records rather than glosses:
**no execution evidence exists in the repository.** The scripts are internally consistent and would
run; that they *were* run is not established. See [[oracle-database-laboratories]].

## Why a client gets its own page

Because the run contract lives here, not in the database. `@`-ordered scripts with no build step and
no driver program are the same delivery shape as [[zero-dependency-no-build-step]] elsewhere in this
source set: the artefact is text, the runner is whatever the reader already has, and the ordering is
carried by [[numbered-stages-in-directory-names]] rather than by a manifest.
